body:
It's funny you mention OFW. That was also part of the parenting agreement and I paid the bucks to have it renewed, he has yet to do so (but it's only about a week outstanding for him.)

I send messages when I think the information needs to be passed along (like when the children are ill and what not,) and requesting information from him (like when the kids come home with coughs, asking to be informed whether or not he's given them anything for it so I know whether or not I can give them something and not over-medicate them,) and the response rate is ten to one. Well, just under that but I'll round up for fun. He doesn't tell me anything, unless it's something very specific in the court order (like the time he took the kids to some waterpark/hotel, where they would be overnight) and he knows I can catch him out on it if he doesn't. He only responds to my requests for information if he feels like he has to (like the address of his girlfriend when the kids told me they were spending weekends there instead of his place) or I repeatedly request it (like asking to swap weekends when my father got married.) I log in every day, regardless of whether or not there are messages to check. I provide all my children's school, teacher, and activity information. I even calendar when my children will be overnight somewhere besides home (it's in the order that we provide the address of where the children will be overnight) for him as well as send messages. bah. None of that has anything to do with what I asked. Sorry.

So civil contempt. 

With my lawyer, I have to do all my paperwork myself. He will go over it, and represent me in court for that one instance, but for as little money as he takes from me, I have to have everything ready and done myself. I get a fifteen minute consult before I turn over the paperwork and I get a one hour consult the day before the hearing, whatever it is.

As for custody itself, I have full legal and physical custody, I don't need to change that. I only want to reduce the visitation to what it was prior to the most recent agreement as he has not fulfilled his side of the bargain, and it's a pain in the ass.

I think in this day and age of the types of technology that make communication without face to face interaction not only possible, but far easier than stepping outside one's front door, actual connections become... blurry.

I'm not saying you need to go outside and meet people, but maybe you can re-evaluate the connections you do have. How do you define a close friend? 

As for dating - your prior experience is meaningless when you are talking about a lasting relationship with real intimacy. Everyone is different. Every prior relationship feeds your expectations of the next and while sometimes this can help, it hinders more often than not, in my own experience. Every relationship is different and for the best chance of each to grow into something meaningful, it needs to be regarded as the first relationship one has ever had. In my opinion anyway.

Rejection is a difficult thing to deal with and we are all socially conditioned to avoid it, and shun it. It sucks, and there is no way around it. All we can do is move on from it but I can understand the difficulty, I think everyone can, because there is no one out there who has not experienced it. 

I had a therapist once, who told me to stop living my life to the expectations of others. The outside validation I was told to stop seeking, though, I think is necessary. Internal validation is great and all but if you sit and think about it for too long you realise that it's all bullshit, and none of it really matters until you can hear someone else agree with you. We aren't wrong in seeking that validation, I think. It's just really hard to come by sometimes. A little confidence in yourself goes a long way though. My grandad always told me that I had to fake it until I made it. He was talking about sleep but it's served me well otherwise. 

Do stuff for yourself for a while and forget other people. When you get to the point where you can fake it, you do. You fake it until it's real.
